pr.title: Refuse a released or older version before opening the release pull request
pr.head: ec3e7e455747511cc54444a87d000596b2230898

summary: trip releases through a GitHub Actions workflow, release.yml, with two jobs. You start the propose job by hand with patch, minor, or major. It raises the version in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock on a release/vX.Y.Z branch and opens a pull request. When that pull request merges, the publish job tags vX.Y.Z, creates the GitHub release, and moves v0, the tag the installer follows.

The problem is a revert. Reverting a release pull request sets main back to the older version, say from 0.6.0 to 0.5.0. The next propose run then bumps from 0.5.0: a patch bump proposes 0.5.1, below the released 0.6.0, and a minor bump proposes 0.6.0, which is already released. Before this change the propose job opened that pull request anyway, its checks passed, and only the publish job refused it, after someone had merged it. That left main on a version that could not be released.

This change adds a check-version command to .github/scripts/release.py and runs it in the propose job right after the bump, before anything is committed or pushed. It reads the remote's vX.Y.Z tags and refuses a version at or below the newest one, with a message that says to set a higher version with release.py set. The comparison lives in one helper, check_unreleased, which the publish job's tag command now calls too, so the two checks cannot drift apart.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Released version: one that has a vX.Y.Z tag on origin. v0 and tags such as v0.6.0-rc1 do not count.
  • Newest release: the highest of those versions by number, not by date.
  • Propose job: the hand-started job that opens the release pull request.
  • Publish job: the job that runs on a push to main that changes Cargo.toml, and tags and publishes the release.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: One Projector review of ec3e7e4: clean, no finding threads, and one suggestion to reword a comment in check_unreleased whose reason predates this change.

groups.title: The version check in release.py
groups.kicker: A new check-version command and the helper it shares with tag
intro: release.py is the script both workflow jobs call. This group adds the check itself. check_unreleased takes a version and the list of released versions, and raises ReleaseError when the version is at or below the newest. check_version reads the version from the checkout's files and the released versions from origin, and calls it. main wires it up as the check-version subcommand, which prints a one-line result or exits 1 with a release: message.
The publish job's merged function had the same comparison inline. It now calls check_unreleased, so its refusal gains the same release.py set hint.

files.note: Adds check_unreleased and check_version, the check-version subcommand, and docstring lines that describe it; merged now calls the shared helper.

checks.text: The comparison is now at-or-below, where merged used strictly-below. merged calls it only when the version's own tag is absent from origin, so it cannot be equal to a released version there, and tag's behavior is unchanged. Checked by reading merged and by running TagTests, which pass.

This comment moved here from merged unchanged. Its reason predates the change and is weaker than it reads, since tag already leaves the major tag on a newer release (line 318). The review lists rewording it as a suggestion.

tagged_versions reads origin with git ls-remote --tags --refs, so the propose job's shallow checkout needs no tag fetch, and a tag that exists only locally does not count. test_reads_the_tags_the_remote_has_not_the_checkouts covers the second point.

groups.title: The propose job runs the check
groups.kicker: Where the check sits in release.yml, and what the generated pull request says
intro: The propose job's run step already starts with set -euo pipefail, so any command that exits non-zero stops it. The new line runs check-version right after bump writes the new version, and before the job switches to the release branch, commits, pushes, or opens the pull request. A refused version therefore leaves nothing on GitHub; the bumped files on the runner are discarded with it.

files.note: Runs check-version after bump, and updates the header comment and the body of the pull request the job opens.

checks.text: Placed before git switch, git commit, git push, and gh pr create. WorkflowTests fails when this line is removed, which the review checked by replacing it and running the test.
The comment's claim holds: a minor bump back to a released 0.6.0 reaches check_tagged in the publish job, which refuses it because 0.5.0 sits between the tag and the head in history.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: CheckVersionTests against a temporary origin, and a workflow ordering test
intro: CheckVersionTests builds a temporary bare repository that stands in for origin, pushes tags to it, writes a version into the clone's files, and runs check-version through main, asserting the exit code and the exact output. The cases are the two revert outcomes (0.5.1 and 0.6.0 under v0.6.0), a version above every release and the first release, tags that name no release, and a tag that exists only locally. WorkflowTests reads release.yml and checks that bump, check-version, the commit, the push, and gh pr create appear in that order.

checks.text: All 29 tests in tests/release_test.py pass. Weakening the check to strictly-below fails test_refuses_a_bump_to_a_version_already_tagged.

groups.title: README
groups.kicker: The Releasing section describes the earlier refusal and how to recover
intro: The README's Releasing section now says the workflow refuses an already-released or older version before it opens the pull request, and what to do then: write a higher version with release.py set X.Y.Z and open that change as a pull request yourself. Merging it publishes that version, because the publish job releases any push that raises the version.

checks.text: The completed releases plan still says the propose job would open a pull request the publish job refuses. A completed plan is a record of what was built, so the README is the document this change keeps current.
